## Why This Is Asked
This question explores a dynamic sequence with range-frequency queries, introducing a new angle not covered by the existing questions. It teaches augmenting a balanced tree and split/merge techniques for range queries.

## Key Concepts
- Implicit treap
- Subtree frequency arrays
- Range queries via split/merge
- Amortized O(log n) updates

## Code Example
```javascript
class Node { constructor(chIndex){ this.chIndex=chIndex; this.pri=Math.random(); this.left=null; this.right=null; this.size=1; this.freq=new Array(26).fill(0); this.freq[chIndex]=1; } }
function upd(t){ if(!t) return; t.size=1; t.freq.fill(0); if(t.left){ t.size+=t.left.size; for(let i=0;i<26;i++) t.freq[i]+=t.left.freq[i]; } if(t.right){ t.size+=t.right.size; for(let i=0;i<26;i++) t.freq[i]+=t.right.freq[i]; } t.freq[t.chIndex]+=1; }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this to larger alphabets efficiently?
- How would you test correctness with random operations and a naive baseline?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical rope design for fast text editing and substring equality checks at scale—a core requirement in code editors and compilers.

## Key Concepts

- **Implicit treap (rope)**: A binary search tree keyed by position rather than explicit indices, combining BST properties with heap priority for randomized balancing
- **Subtree size maintenance**: Essential for O(log n) index-based operations; updated bottom-up after each modification
- **Rolling hash with precomputed powers**: Enables O(log n) substring hashing via temporary splits; base powers are precomputed up to maximum document length for O(1) multiplication
- **Collision mitigation**: Using 2^64 modulus provides natural overflow behavior; for higher confidence, pair with a second independent hash function or use modulo with large primes

## Data Structure Design

Each node contains:
- `char`: the character value
- `size`: aggregate subtree size for index navigation
- `hash`: rolling hash of the subtree
- `priority`: random value for heap property
- `left`, `right`: child pointers

## Operations

- **insertAt(i, s)**: Split treap at position i, merge left + new nodes + right
- **deleteAt(i, len)**: Split at i, then split again at i+len to isolate deletion range, merge remaining parts
- **substringHash(l, r)**: Split at r, then at l-1 to isolate range, extract hash, re-merge
- **equalSubstring(l1, r1, l2, r2)**: Compare hash values of both ranges in O(log n)

## Complexity

All operations run in O(log n) time due to treap splitting/merging, making this suitable for code editors handling long documents with frequent insertions, deletions, and substring queries.

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates a candidate's ability to design hybrid data structures that support dynamic 2D range queries with an additional color dimension, a common requirement in spatial analytics and geographic information systems.

## Key Concepts
- Dynamic 2D range structures (segment trees, range trees)
- Per-node multisets for color tracking and distinct counting
- Coordinate compression for memory efficiency
- Duplicate handling via color frequency counters
- Trade-offs between memory usage and query performance
- Lazy rebuilding strategies for coordinate space optimization

## Code Example
```javascript
// Sketch: insertPoint updates across O(log n) x-nodes,
// adjusting per-node y-color maps and distinct color counters
function insertPoint(x, y, color) {
  const compressedX = compressCoordinate(x);
  updateSegmentTree(compressedX, y, color, 1);
}
```

## Follow-up Considerations
